source.anchor: One actual-law Gaussian polynomial ridge theorem and four mathematical proof steps
source.original_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure, and p any real polynomial. Put phi(z)=p(z), gamma1=N(0,1), gammaE=stdGaussian(E), and U={w in E: norm(w)=1}. Then phi genuinely belongs to L2(gamma1). Define b=norm(phi)_{L2(gamma1)}+1. One has b>0, and every actual ridge x↦phi(<w,x>) for w in U genuinely belongs to L2(gammaE), with norm exactly norm(phi)_{L2(gamma1)} and hence at most b. The one base norm and the same b serve every direction and dimension. Neither positive dimension, a nonzero polynomial nor evenness is required; the feature conclusions are vacuous when U is empty. No feature moment, covariance or uniform bound is assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem result
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) :
    let phi : ℝ → ℝ := fun z => p.eval z
    ∃ hbase : MemLp phi 2 (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1),
      let b : ℝ := ‖hbase.toLp phi‖ + 1
      (0 < b) ∧
      ∃ hfeature : ∀ w : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1},
        MemLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ) 2 (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E),
        ∀ w : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1},
          ‖(hfeature w).toLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ)‖ = ‖hbase.toLp phi‖ ∧
          ‖(hfeature w).toLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ)‖ ≤ b

blind_reconstruction.text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E equipped with a measurable-space structure equal to its Borel structure, and every real polynomial p, let phi:R->R be the actual function phi(z)=p.eval(z). Let gamma1 be gaussianReal(0,1), the actual one-dimensional standard Gaussian, and gammaE be stdGaussian(E), the actual centered identity-covariance standard Gaussian on E. Then there exists a witness hbase of MemLp(phi,2,gamma1). For that witness define b=norm(hbase.toLp(phi))+1. This b is strictly positive. Moreover, there exists a single family hfeature witnessing, for every w in the subtype U={w:E | norm(w)=1}, MemLp(x->phi(inner_product(w,x)),2,gammaE). For that family, for every w in U, both norm((hfeature(w)).toLp(x->phi(inner_product(w,x))))=norm(hbase.toLp(phi)) and norm((hfeature(w)).toLp(x->phi(inner_product(w,x))))<=b hold, with the feature norm under gammaE and base norm under gamma1. MemLp and all of the membership witnesses are conclusions rather than supplied integrability assumptions; they assert almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm of the displayed actual functions. The toLp constructions are the genuine equivalence classes of those fixed functions, not choices of alternative functions or laws. The same base witness, the b defined from its norm, and the single feature-witness family serve every unit direction; b does not vary with w. Semantically the base norm and b depend only on p and the fixed gamma1 law, not on the witness proof, E, or direction. The exact equality identifies the norm of each polynomial ridge with the one-dimensional norm, whereas the inequality supplies the larger common positive bound b. Since norms are nonnegative, the definition also gives b>=1, although the explicit positivity claim is b>0. No nonzero polynomial, positive degree, or positive-dimension assumption is imposed. If p is the zero polynomial, phi and every ridge are zero, their L2 norms are zero, and b=1. If E has dimension zero, there are no unit vectors, so the feature-membership family and its universally quantified equality and bound are vacuous, while the base membership and positivity of b remain asserted. No analogous statement for nonunit weights or a global pointwise bound on the polynomial features is claimed.

import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space
import Mathlib.Analysis.Polynomial.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped ENNReal InnerProductSpace

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialRidge

theorem standard_gaussian_polynomial_ridge_uniform_L2
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) :
    let phi : ℝ → ℝ := fun z => p.eval z
    ∃ hbase : MemLp phi 2 (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1),
      let b : ℝ := ‖hbase.toLp phi‖ + 1
      (0 < b) ∧
      ∃ hfeature : ∀ w : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1},
        MemLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ) 2 (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E),
        ∀ w : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1},
          ‖(hfeature w).toLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ)‖ = ‖hbase.toLp phi‖ ∧
          ‖(hfeature w).toLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ)‖ ≤ b := by
  let phi : ℝ → ℝ := fun z => p.eval z
  have hpow : ∀ n : ℕ,
      MemLp (fun z : ℝ => z ^ n) 2 (gaussianReal 0 1) := by
    intro n
    apply (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq (by fun_prop)).2
    have hid : MemLp (id : ℝ → ℝ) (↑(2 * n) : ℝ≥0∞) (gaussianReal 0 1) :=
      memLp_id_gaussianReal' (↑(2 * n) : ℝ≥0∞) (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top (2 * n))
    have hi := hid.integrable_norm_pow' (p := 2 * n)
    convert hi using 1
    funext z
    change (z ^ n) ^ 2 = ‖z‖ ^ (2 * n)
    rw [Nat.mul_comm 2 n, pow_mul, ← norm_pow, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs]
  have hbase : MemLp phi 2 (gaussianReal 0 1) := by
    change MemLp (fun z : ℝ => p.eval z) 2 (gaussianReal 0 1)
    induction p using Polynomial.induction_on' with
    | add p q hp hq => simpa only [Polynomial.eval_add, Pi.add_def] using hp.add hq
    | monomial n a => simpa only [Polynomial.eval_monomial] using (hpow n).const_mul a
  have hmap : ∀ w : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1},
      (stdGaussian E).map (fun x : E => ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ) = gaussianReal 0 1 := by
    intro w
    change (stdGaussian E).map (innerSL ℝ w.1) = _
    rw [IsGaussian.map_eq_gaussianReal, integral_strongDual_stdGaussian,
      variance_dual_stdGaussian, innerSL_apply_norm, w.2]
    norm_num
  let mp : ∀ w : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1},
      MeasurePreserving (fun x : E => ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ) (stdGaussian E) (gaussianReal 0 1) :=
    fun w => ⟨by fun_prop, hmap w⟩
  let hfeature : ∀ w : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1},
      MemLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ) 2 (stdGaussian E) :=
    fun w => hbase.comp_measurePreserving (mp w)
  refine ⟨hbase, ?_, hfeature, ?_⟩
  · exact add_pos_of_nonneg_of_pos (norm_nonneg _) zero_lt_one
  · intro w
    have hn : ‖(hfeature w).toLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ)‖ = ‖hbase.toLp phi‖ := by
      change ‖Lp.compMeasurePreserving (fun x : E => ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ) (mp w)
        (hbase.toLp phi)‖ = ‖hbase.toLp phi‖
      exact Lp.norm_compMeasurePreserving _ _
    exact ⟨hn, hn.trans_le (le_add_of_nonneg_right zero_le_one)⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialRidge

steps.title: Produce polynomial moments
steps.text: The actual scalar Gaussian has every finite moment. Thus z^n belongs to L2 since its squared absolute value is |z|^(2n). Finite polynomial induction, addition and coefficient scaling produce L2 membership of phi; no moment premise is introduced.
steps.lean: The adjacent initially folded Lean contains the exact statement and proof of this step.

steps.title: Identify the actual projection law
steps.text: A continuous linear functional of the standard Gaussian is Gaussian with mean zero and variance equal to its squared dual norm. The inner-product functional at a unit vector has norm one, so the pushforward is exactly gamma1.
steps.lean: The adjacent initially folded Lean contains the exact statement and proof of this step.

steps.title: Transport the genuine L2 class
steps.text: This measurable projection preserves the indicated measures. Pull back phi and its actual almost-everywhere class. The induced L2 pullback is an isometry, proving membership and equality of norms simultaneously.
steps.lean: The adjacent initially folded Lean contains the exact statement and proof of this step.

steps.title: Choose one positive common bound
steps.text: A norm is nonnegative, so adding one makes b strictly positive. The exact isometry gives the same bound for every unit weight, with no dimension or direction in its definition.
steps.lean: The adjacent initially folded Lean contains the exact statement and proof of this step.
